title: Catch OEE losses before they happen
subtitle:
IT + OT on one Databricks platform · turbine-component plant
FEBAR build · Narasimhan Raam, Sr. Solutions Architect

title: The outcome, per line, per year
subtitle: One 12-asset line, base case (assumptions on slide 8)
body:
+1.0 OEE point (range +0.7 to +1.7) by fixing degradation before it becomes a breakdown
~500 fewer unplanned downtime hours and ~2,500 fewer scrapped parts
≈ $2.75M a year (range $1.0M to $7.7M), before secondary-damage and throughput upside
Failures flagged 57–86 h ahead; the model beats today's rule (precision 0.82 vs 0.67)
Supervisor acted 1.5 min after the alert, with procedure, parts and work order ready

title: Where OEE is lost: the hidden 13 %
data: 63 h, including all 10 breakdowns (5.3 h each)
Closing these windows alone is worth +2.4 points

title: One data journey, one asset key
data: 1.9 M historian readings, SCADA states/alarms, ERP/MES orders and CMMS work orders; 9 quality rules drop bad sensor data and impossible counts
IT / OT / gold domains with owner + steward tags, certified gold OEE, operator PII masked, lineage from raw files to OEE
Next-shift OEE-at-risk model with SHAP drivers; LLM drafts root cause + work order grounded on past repairs
Sub-millisecond at-risk queue for the app; supervisor actions written back and synced to the lakehouse
Genie + Agent Bricks Supervisor + Knowledge Assistant
Plain-English OEE analytics, risk, and repair manuals in one agent; evaluated with MLflow LLM judges
OEE board, at-risk queue, Acknowledge / Create work order, agent chat with human approval for actions

title: On the floor: CNC-02 before failure
subtitle: What the supervisor sees and does
body:
Signal: vibration 6.0 mm/s, +1.8 vs the last 6 shifts; 8 alarms; OEE down to 52 %
Prediction: 99.8 % risk of next-shift OEE < 65 %; top driver is the vibration trend
Cause: likely spindle-bearing wear from lubrication starvation (4 similar past repairs)
Plan: procedure MM-CNC-01-R7 (6 h), pre-stage bearing set SP-BRG-7014-P4, P1 at next planned stop
Action: agent raises the request only after the user approves; supervisor approves the work order
Loop closed in Unity Catalog: first action 1.5 min after the alert

title: Proof: model and agent, measured
data: Today's rule: flag if this shift's OEE < 65 %
Warning before the 3 breakdowns in the window
Agent eval: 10 plant questions, MLflow judges

title: Business value per 12-asset line, per year
data: Key assumption (to replace with plant data)
72 % of windows caught; 60 % of each window's loss recovered
$2.5k–$10k per unplanned hour on a constrained cell; planned hour = 30 %
excludes secondary damage, throughput, MTTR gains

title: Trust by design
bodies:
IT, OT and gold domains, each with an owner and a steward
Operator names and badges masked outside the HR group
Lineage from historian file to the OEE number
App identity limited to the 7 tables, 2 functions, 2 endpoints and 1 Genie space it needs

Model registered with a signature; drivers shown per asset
Answers grounded on plant data and manuals, procedure IDs cited
Agent actions need two human approvals: tool call, then work order
Every question and action logged and synced back for audit

title: Roadmap and the ask
data: One line: real historian tags + SCADA states, ERP/MES orders, CMMS work orders; asset key map
Daily OEE per asset and shift matches the plant's report within ±1 point
Retrain on 6–12 months of history; add manuals; pilot app with one shift team
Precision ≥ 0.75 on held-out weeks; supervisors act on alerts within 1 hour (SOP)
Run in production on the line; track planned vs unplanned stops
Measured OEE and downtime change vs baseline; go / no-go for plant rollout
Sponsor: approve a 90-day pilot on one line. Domain owner: name a pilot shift team and the reliability engineer
Plant data access (historian, MES, CMMS) granted in week 1
